 Edited by Aastha Jha / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 20, 2026, 15:18 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small

 Print Congress leaders criticised the Centre over Pakistan minister Masood Malik's visit to Delhi for the SCO Civilisation Dialogue NEW DELHI: A political row broke out after Pakistan minister Masood Malik arrived in Delhi on Friday to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue. Congress questioned the invitation and accused the BJP-led Centre of “rubbing salt into the wounds of Pahalgam victims’ families”. "You keep changing your stance. Sometimes you travel there, sometimes you reach Lahore, at other times you abruptly call off Operation Sindoor, and now you invite them here. What exactly is Prime Minister Modi doing? The funeral pyres of those martyred in the Pahalgam massacre have not even cooled yet, and you are rubbing salt into the wounds of their families,” said Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate. "The Government of India, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is organising the SCO Civilisational Dialogue in India on November 21 and 22. The question is: why was Pakistan invited to this event? Why have you invited Pakistan, a country that sponsors terrorism in India? You invited Pakistan, and its minister, Musadik Malik, has arrived here," she said. Questioning the "red carpet" treatment being extended to the minister, Shrinate said, "This is the same person who had openly threatened just a few months ago to chop off the hands of Indians and shed our blood." "The question is that Pakistan has not stopped sponsoring terrorism, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government is busy welcoming its representatives. Musadik Malik be served biryani, kebabs and kheer? The government is rolling out the red carpet to welcome him. Why does your work not get done without an anti-India Pakistan? The point is that you should also say and do what Rahul Gandhi has stated unequivocally: as long as Pakistan continues to sponsor terrorism, no dialogue with it is possible," she added. J&K Congress President Tariq Hameed Karra also accused the BJP of having "double standards" regarding militancy, Indo-Pakistan talks, or international treaties. "Look, as far as the Government of India is concerned, particularly the BJP, th ey have always had double standards. Whether it is regarding militancy, Indo-Pakistan talks, or international treaties, their approach has consistently been marked by double standards. The very person who made the loudest protests when the Indus Waters Treaty was suspended here had raised more objections than anyone else at that time. But the fact that they are displaying double standards is nothing new," he said. "This is another example of their double standards. When our Prime Minister went to Pakistan uninvited, what could be a bigger example of double standards than that? Basically, the BJP has lost its track. Join conversation

 Its foreign policy is being handled on a day-to-day basis. It has no consistent or permanent policy towards its neighbouring countries, whether Pakistan, China, Bangladesh or Sri Lanka. They deal with each country according to what suits them at a particular time," he added. Pakistan's federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination Masood Malik arrived in New Delhi to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue. He was received by Pakistan high commissioner's Chargé d'Affaires in India, Saad Warraich. Malik's visit marks the first time a Pakistani minister has travelled to India in three years.
